assessments.scope:
Accounts Payable asked for approval to keep using a macro-enabled Excel workbook that matches supplier invoices against purchase orders exported from the finance system.

In scope: the workbook, its macros, where it is stored and who can change it. Out of scope: the finance system itself.

Test data with made-up details and people.
assessments.summaryComments: The workbook was reviewed as an in-house custom program for 40 Accounts Payable users. Its macros read two exported files and write a matching report; they make no network connections and do not call other programs. The solution risk level is Medium, driven by unsigned macros and the absence of change control. With the macros signed and the workbook kept in a controlled library, residual risk is Low. Cyber Risk does not object to continued use on those terms.
assessments.solutionOverview:
A macro-enabled workbook stored on the Finance shared drive. Staff export purchase orders and invoices from the finance system as CSV files, the macros match them and highlight differences, and the result is saved as a new workbook for the month-end file.

The macros were written by a former analyst. The workbook holds supplier names, invoice amounts and bank reference numbers.
assessments.topRisks:
The macros are unsigned, so staff are used to enabling macros on prompt, which also works for malicious files.
Anyone with access to the shared folder can change the macro code, and there is no record of changes.
Only one person understands the code, and it has no documentation.
Monthly output files with supplier bank references build up on the shared drive with no retention rule.

recommendations.recommendation: Sign the macros with the company code-signing certificate and store the workbook in a trusted location, so unsigned macros can stay blocked.
recommendations.treatment: Signed on 21 October 2026 by End User Computing. Implemented.

recommendations.recommendation: Move the master workbook to a library where only two named owners can edit it, with version history turned on.
recommendations.treatment: Moved to the Finance controlled library on 23 October 2026. Implemented.

recommendations.recommendation: Document what each macro does and name a second maintainer.
recommendations.treatment: Documentation due 30 November 2026. Second maintainer named.

recommendations.recommendation: Apply the finance retention rule to the monthly output files.
recommendations.treatment: Accepted by the Controller until the shared drive migration in 2027, when retention labels become available.

handoff.team: CFC – Endpoint Desktop Services / Device Management
handoff.actions: Sign the macros and set the trusted location.
Restrict edit rights to the two owners.

assessments.scope:
Corporate Communications asked for a cloud assistant that joins online meetings, records them, and produces a transcript, summary and action list.

In scope: the vendor's cloud service, its calendar and meeting integrations, and how recordings and transcripts are stored and shared. Out of scope: the meeting platform itself.

Test data with made-up details and people.
assessments.solutionOverview:
A subscription cloud service. Each user connects their calendar, and the assistant joins their meetings automatically as a participant. Audio is transcribed and summarised by the vendor's AI models, and the results are emailed to all invitees by default.

Recordings and transcripts are stored in the vendor's cloud. The vendor's standard terms allow customer content to be used to improve its models unless the customer opts out.
assessments.topRisks:
The assistant joins every meeting on a connected calendar by default, including legal, HR and board meetings.
Transcripts and summaries are emailed to all invitees, including people outside the company.
Customer content may be used to train the vendor's models under the standard terms.
The vendor has not yet provided an independent security report.
It is not yet known whether engineering staff who discuss protected operational information would be in the user population.
AI summaries can be wrong, and may be relied on as the record of a decision.

recommendations.recommendation: Sign the enterprise agreement with the model-training opt-out and a 90-day retention limit before any use.
Require single sign-on, and turn off automatic joining so the assistant attends only when the organiser invites it.
Restrict sharing of transcripts to internal participants, and exclude legal, HR and board meetings by policy.
Obtain the vendor's current independent security report and complete a vendor review.
Keep engineering and operations staff out of the user population until it is confirmed that no protected operational information is discussed in recorded meetings.
recommendations.treatment: Agreed with the requestor: these groups are excluded from the pilot.

recommendations.recommendation: Tell users that summaries are drafts to be checked by the meeting organiser before they are circulated.

handoff.team: CFC – Endpoint Desktop Services / Device Management

assessments.scope:
Protection Engineering asked for a desktop tool that compares protection relay settings files against the approved baseline.

In scope: installation on twelve engineering laptops, how settings files are brought to the laptop, and where results are stored. Out of scope: any direct connection from the tool to relays or substation networks, which is not requested.

Test data with made-up details and people.
assessments.summaryComments: The tool was reviewed as commercial desktop software for twelve protection engineers. It works on settings files copied to the laptop and does not connect to relays. NERC CIP applies because the settings files are protected information and the laptops are used as transient devices. The solution risk level is High. Cyber Risk does not object provided the compliance review is completed and the storage and removable media conditions below are met before installation.
assessments.solutionOverview:
A Windows desktop application. An engineer opens two settings files, and the tool lists every difference and produces a comparison report as a PDF. It supports the file formats of the three relay vendors in use.

It runs offline. Licence activation needs one outbound connection to the vendor at installation.
assessments.topRisks:
Relay settings files are protected information, and comparison reports copy parts of them into PDFs that are easy to email or misfile.
Settings files reach the laptop on removable media.
The engineering laptops connect to substation equipment, so new software on them needs compliance review and a recorded baseline change.
The vendor releases updates about twice a year, and older versions stop receiving fixes.

recommendations.recommendation: Complete the compliance review and record the software in the laptop baseline before installation.
Save settings files and comparison reports only to the approved protected-information repository, never to the laptop's local drive or email.
recommendations.treatment: Report output folder will be fixed by configuration. Procedure update due 5 December 2026.

recommendations.recommendation: Bring settings files to the laptop only on scanned, company-issued removable media.
recommendations.treatment: Already required by the transient device procedure.

recommendations.recommendation: Apply vendor updates within 35 days of release, following the existing patch assessment process.
recommendations.treatment: Added to the engineering software patch list.

recommendations.recommendation: Allow the one-time licence activation through a temporary firewall rule, then remove it.
recommendations.treatment: Activation will be done by the vendor's offline licence file instead, so no firewall rule is needed.

handoff.actions: Raise the installation request once the compliance review is signed.

handoff.team: CFC – Endpoint Desktop Services / Device Management
handoff.actions: Install on the twelve named laptops only.
Add to the engineering patch list.
Track the two open treatment plans.

assessments.scope:
The Training team asked for a browser extension to capture and annotate screenshots for user guides.

Test data with made-up details and people.
assessments.summaryComments: The extension was reviewed as freeware for 85 users in the Training team. It captures the visible tab only when the user clicks its button, stores images locally and has no cloud upload feature. The solution risk level is Low. Cyber Risk does not object to its use when deployed from the managed extension list with automatic updates.
assessments.solutionOverview: A browser extension that captures the current tab, lets the user add arrows, boxes and text, and saves the image to the Downloads folder. It asks for permission to read the active tab on click, and nothing else.
assessments.topRisks:
Extensions update automatically, and a future version could ask for wider permissions or change owner.
Screenshots of internal systems may include confidential data.

recommendations.recommendation: Deploy through the managed extension list pinned to the reviewed publisher, and review again if the extension asks for new permissions.
recommendations.treatment: Added to the managed list on 24 September 2026. Permission changes are blocked until reviewed.

recommendations.recommendation: Remind the Training team to blur confidential data in screenshots used in guides.
recommendations.treatment: Covered by the existing documentation standard.

handoff.team: CFC – Endpoint Desktop Services / Device Management
handoff.actions: Added to the managed extension list.
